SPACETIME LAB

INTERACTIVE SCIENCE PROJECT

Gravity bends space.
This project lets you see it.

Instead of showing gravity as a hole in a flat sheet, the simulation uses one transparent 3D grid. Sagittarius A*, the Sun and every planet deform that same continuous space according to their mass.

UNDERSTAND IN 30 SECONDS

What is the simulation showing?

01

Mass changes geometry

In general relativity, gravity is described as curvature of spacetime. The grid is a visual guide for that geometry.

02

More mass, more curvature

Earth bends the grid a little, Jupiter more, the Sun much more, and Sagittarius A* dominates the galactic scale.

03

Objects follow curved paths

Planets are not pulled by an invisible rope. They move through curved spacetime, which appears to us as an orbit.

i

The grid is a teaching visualization, not a literal material in space. Distances and deformation amplitudes are stylized so the effect remains visible on screen.

DESIGN & DEVELOPMENT

How the project evolved

The visual model was refined step by step to make the gravity easier to read without turning the scene into a forest of lines.

WHAT CHANGED

Improvements made along the way

✓

Flat “rubber-sheet” representation removed.

✓

Transparent grid extended through the 3D volume.

✓

Local mini-grids replaced by one continuous deformation field.

✓

Sun, Jupiter, Saturn, Earth and smaller planets contribute with different visual strength.

✓

Camera can smoothly migrate between the Sun, Earth, Sagittarius A* and other bodies.

✓

Interface supports English, German and French.
